cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama House of Representatives for District 41 since October 2016, after winning a special election. Owns and operates Ellis Properties Inc., a real estate brokerage. Previously served as a Shelby County Commissioner. Holds a B.S. and an MBA from Auburn University.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Corley Ellis was born or raised, or when he came to Alabama. We found no bills he sponsored, no deeds in office on the listed issues, and no public statements on them. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 or 2022 candidate surveys, and no campaign platform was available. We found no stated positions on data centers or development, no documented controversies, no foreign ties and no endorsements. The dates he served as Shelby County Commissioner were not given.

qual.background: Alabama House member since October 2016 (re-elected 2018, 2022 and 2026), former Shelby County Commissioner for District 1, and owner of the real estate brokerage Ellis Properties Inc. He holds a B.S. in business administration (1993) and an MBA (1995) from Auburn.
qual.why: He has about ten years of prior legislative service, plus local elected office, business ownership and an MBA. Committee posts, including the Insurance Committee chair, were not counted.

cands.bio: Democratic candidate for Alabama House District 41 in 2026. He advanced from the canceled Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot. No information about his occupation or prior offices was found in the sources available.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving voter guide recommendations from Tabitha's List: Candidates You Can Trust (a Sway voting group by Tabitha Isner) and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy (a Sway voting group by Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not find where David Morgan was born or raised, when he came to Alabama, or his occupation and work history. He has held no office we could document. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and we found no campaign site statements, interviews or questionnaires on his positions. We found no documented stances on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing, and no documented controversies or foreign ties.

score.why: Raised $3,716, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
